reasoning_traces.think:
The triad of runway configuration, capacity change, and flight quantity predictors constitutes a hierarchical temporal forecasting system. Runway configuration predictor (310) generates 12 predictions per scenario across 100 scenarios = 1,200 total configurations. Capacity change predictor (320) evaluates these against historical demand and slot availability to identify capacity shift times. Flight quantity predictor (330) then estimates magnitude of flight volume changes at those times. These components interact through shared inputs—historical weather and operations data—and are scored post-smoothing by capacity smoother (400). The system exhibits dualities: (1) spatial-temporal duality between runway layout and capacity dynamics, and (2) predictive duality between configuration and quantity changes. Failure modes include overfitting due to limited historical data, misalignment between predicted and actual slot usage, and sensitivity to noise in demand estimation.
